key_facts: Morphogenesis encompasses growth, ecdysis, tissue differentiation, and reproductive maturation.
Four stages: Egg (embryogenesis), Immature (larva/nymph), Pupa (transitory remodeling), Adult (imago).
Instar is the physical form between moults; stadium is the elapsed time duration.
Ametabolous: Primitive Apterygota (Silverfish); 3 stages (egg, young, adult); wingless; <0.1% of species.
Hemimetabolous: Exopterygota (Orthoptera, Hemiptera); 3 stages (egg, nymph, adult); external wing pads; ~12% of species.
Holometabolous: Endopterygota (Lepidoptera, Coleoptera, Diptera); 4 stages (egg, larva, pupa, adult); internal wing discs; ~88% of species.

topics.mindmap_node: Chapter 11: Metamorphosis > 3. Immature & Pupal Classifications > 3.1 Larval Types
key_facts: Eruciform: Caterpillar-like, thoracic legs + 2-5 abdominal prolegs with crochets (Lepidoptera).
Scarabaeiform: C-shaped grub, well-developed head & thoracic legs, no prolegs (Scarabaeidae).
Campodeiform: Flattened, active predator with long thoracic legs and cerci (Carabidae, Neuroptera).
Elateriform: Wireworm-like, cylindrical, heavily sclerotized, short legs (Elateridae).
Vermiform: Apodous legless maggot with eucephalous, hemicephalous, or acephalous head capsules (Diptera).

topics.mindmap_node: Chapter 11: Metamorphosis > 3. Immature & Pupal Classifications > 3.2 Pupal Types
key_facts: Exarate: Appendages free and unattached to body (Coleoptera, Hymenoptera).
Obtect: Appendages glued tightly to body in a chrysalis (Lepidoptera).
Coarctate: Enclosed inside hardened barrel-shaped 4th/5th larval puparium (Diptera).
Decticous vs Adecticous: Functional articulated mandibles vs non-functional mandibles.
Complete metamorphosis with two or more distinct larval forms during development.
Classical cycle in Meloidae (Blister beetles): Triungulin -> Grub-like larva -> Coarctate pseudopupa -> Active larva -> Pupa -> Adult.
Triungulin is an active, campodeiform, host-seeking first instar; coarctate is a dormant overwintering instar.
PTTH (brain hormone) from protocerebrum NSCs stimulates prothoracic glands via corpora cardiaca.
Ecdysone from prothoracic glands triggers apolysis, epidermal mitosis, and cuticle secretion.
Juvenile Hormone (JH) from corpora allata dictates moult status: high JH = larva, low JH = pupa, zero JH = adult.

topics.mindmap_node: Chapter 11: Metamorphosis > 6. Diapause & Dormancy > 6.1 Core Concepts
key_facts: Quiescence is an immediate, direct response to unfavorable conditions (resumes immediately upon warmth/water).
Diapause is an internally programmed, genetically governed physiological arrest triggered ahead of time by token stimuli.
Diapause development requires a physiological refractory period before development can resume.

topics.mindmap_node: Chapter 11: Metamorphosis > 6. Diapause & Dormancy > 6.2 & 6.3 Diapause Types
key_facts: Obligatory diapause is genetically fixed in every generation (univoltine species).
Facultative diapause is environmentally induced by token stimuli (multivoltine species).
Hibernation is winter dormancy (cold, short days); Aestivation is summer dormancy (heat, drought, long days).

topics.topic: Photoperiodic Cues, Token Stimuli & Critical Day Length
topics.mindmap_node: Chapter 11: Metamorphosis > 6. Diapause & Dormancy > Token Stimuli
key_facts: Token stimuli (photoperiod) signal oncoming seasonal change with zero direct nutritional impact.
Critical Day Length (CDL) is the exact photoperiod inducing diapause in 50% of the population.
Long-day insects enter hibernation when day length drops below CDL; short-day insects enter aestivation above CDL.

topics.mindmap_node: Chapter 11: Metamorphosis > 6. Diapause & Dormancy > 6.4 Stage Specificity
key_facts: Embryonic diapause: Bombyx mori silkworm, Schistocerca gregaria desert locust.
Larval diapause: Omphisa fuscidentalis bamboo borer, Scirpophaga incertulas rice stem borer, Pectinophora gossypiella pink bollworm.
Pupal diapause: Pieris brassicae cabbage white, Helicoverpa armigera gram pod borer.
Adult/imaginal diapause: Leptinotarsa decemlineata Colorado potato beetle, Aulacophora foveicollis red pumpkin beetle.
